extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing and submitting manuscripts to the American Political Science Review (APSR)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and submission requirements for preparing manuscripts, supplementary materials, and disclosures for submission to the American Political Science Review, including formatting, ethics, reproducibility, and AI declaration rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article types / Format
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines acceptable submission types: Research Articles (original work advancing political science; typically <12,000 words but any length acceptable), Research Notes (shorter, focused), Replications and Reappraisals (revisit prior results), Registered Reports (evaluated prior to data analysis), and Synthesis track (articles providing a synthetic view).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should review the specific guidance for Registered Reports, Synthesis, and Replication/Reappraisal tracks; there is no strict word limit but most articles are <12,000 words; include total word count on front page; abstract must be 150 words or less.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior publication / originality policy
rubrics_metrics.description: APSR publishes only original work; authors must notify editors in the cover letter of any submitted or published work similar or closely related to the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Cambridge's Preprint Policy for exceptions. If overlap exists, disclose in cover letter; failure to disclose may affect review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and reproducibility (DA*RT standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: APSR expects clear, transparent communication about procedures used to collect and analyze evidence and will collaborate with authors to meet DA*RT standards, recognizing diverse methodological approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should make efforts to facilitate evaluation of their claims via data access, production transparency, and analytic transparency whenever legally, ethically, and epistemologically possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of reproducibility packages (conditionally accepted manuscripts)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a conditionally accepted manuscript substantially relies on computations, authors must deposit a reproducibility package containing data, code, and documentation necessary for others to reproduce the manuscript's findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal will verify that the package reproduces the paper's results and is documented sufficiently for future researchers; detailed guidelines for reproducibility packages are provided by the journal. Authors who cannot share data for ethical/legal reasons should contact the editors before review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of formal claims (proofs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers containing formal claims must be submitted with complete proofs in the text or an Online Appendix for reviewers and editors during review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal claims will be reviewed in detail by an editor and assistants at the conditional acceptance stage for consistency and readability; authors are expected to collaborate with the journal to address technical verification issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical obligations (APSA guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must comply with APSA's A Guide to Professional Ethics in Political Science (2012) and Principles and Guidance for Human Subjects Research (2020).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers should (a) ensure human-participant research adheres to APSA principles or provide reasoned justification for deviations; (b) declare compensation to participants and how amounts were determined; (c) declare potential or perceived conflicts of interest; (d) disclose sources of financial support; (e) facilitate evaluation via data access and analytic transparency where possible; and (f) acknowledge contributions including authorship and citations to prior work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission affirmations and screening for ethics/compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting, authors must explicitly affirm how their research practices conform to APSA ethical standards and answer screening questions about human participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the submission draws on research directly engaging human participants, answer 'yes' to the screening question and discuss ethical practices (consent, deception, confidentiality, harm, compensation) in the text or an appendix. Confirm compliance or provide a reasoned justification for deviations; indicate where data collection procedures are described. This information will be shared with reviewers as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and code availability upon acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must confirm that, if the paper is accepted, quantitative data and related code necessary to produce the results will be made publicly available on the APSR Dataverse, or provide a reasoned justification for why this is not possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If confirmation is not possible due to legal, ethical, or methodological constraints, authors must explain and justify these constraints in the text or an appendix at submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript submission compliance (formatting compliance requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must follow manuscript preparation guidelines; manuscripts that do not follow guidelines will be sent back to authors and repeated noncompliance may lead to rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should check all formatting and preparation rules before submission to avoid delays; see detailed sections for specific requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-citation and anonymous review
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts should preserve author anonymity for anonymous review; avoid citing oneself unnecessarily or in ways that reveal identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove obvious references to the author (e.g., 'As I wrote in 1993,...'). Authors may use the APSR Overleaf template to help conform to manuscript format and to manage anonymization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-analysis plans and registrations — share
rubrics_metrics.description: If a study references a pre-analysis plan or pre-registration, authors are expected to include an anonymized version of the registration or a link to an anonymized version in the online appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An anonymized OSF link is an acceptable method. Including the registration in the appendix helps reviewers access it without revealing author identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-analysis plans and registrations — signpost
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must clearly mark which analyses are preregistered and which are unregistered or exploratory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signpost registered vs unregistered analyses in the manuscript; refer to unregistered analyses as 'unregistered' or 'exploratory' so reviewers/readers can distinguish them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-analysis plans and registrations — evaluate
rubrics_metrics.description: In the manuscript, indicate whether results align with preregistered expectations and discuss any differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If preregistrations include expectations, refer to these when discussing findings to help readers assess confirmatory vs exploratory results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-analysis plans and registrations — reconcile deviations
rubrics_metrics.description: If implemented analyses deviate from registered analyses, authors should provide a reconciliation report describing modifications or dropped analyses, justification, and, if possible, what conclusions would have been under original analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place reconciliation details in an appendix and indicate major deviations clearly in the main text. No specific format required, but a reporting table (e.g., Journal for Experimental Political Science style) can be effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript formatting specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Formatting requirements include font, spacing, page numbering, footnote usage, acronyms, and word-count reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Font should be 12 pt for main text and appendices; double-space main text (not necessary for footnotes and references); include page numbers on all pages; use footnotes not endnotes; avoid acronyms or computational abbreviations for variables; include total word-count on front page (main manuscript with footnotes and references, excluding appendices). Abstracts must be 150 words or less.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures and tables placement and description
rubrics_metrics.description: Place figures and tables where they should fall in the manuscript, or use a placeholder like '[Figure/Table 1 about here]', with the figure directly following on a new page. Number figures and tables consecutively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Variables that appear in tables and figures should be described in appropriate detail in the text or appendices. Figures and tables in appendices should be lettered (Table A.1, Figures A.1). Provide captions for all figures and tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure color and grayscale readability
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures should be readable in grayscale; if submitting in color, vary colors by intensity and tone, not just shade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended increments of 15–85% for tonal variation. Note printing in grayscale can make classic blue, black, red and green look the same. Costs of printed color figures are the responsibility of the author.

rubrics_metrics.name: References style and completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: At initial submission any reference style is accepted; after conditional acceptance authors must format references using the 17th Edition of the Chicago Manual of Style (Author-Date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide authors' first and last names (not initials), ensure all listed references are cited in the text and vice versa, include links for non-published work (working papers, conference papers), and ensure publication information is complete and correct at submission. Recommended tools: LaTeX biblatex (chicago-authordate), Zotero CMS 17th author-date, EndNote style provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-text citation format
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Author-Date system in the format (Author Year, Pages) with no comma between author and year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate mass citations with a semicolon. Do not redact self-citations. Do not use footnotes for simple citations. Examples provided in guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendices labeling and pagination
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendices should have descriptive titles, restart the page count, and distinguish between online appendices and those intended for print.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letter figures/tables in appendices (Table A.1, Figure A.1). Provide clear indication which appendices are online-only.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCID requirement for corresponding author
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning January 1, 2019, an ORCID iD is required for corresponding authors submitting to APSR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Editorial Manager system will prompt for ORCID; authors can add it to their profile in advance. Including an ORCID improves discoverability and allows Crossref automatic updates of publication records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility and reliability expectations (post-publication scrutiny)
rubrics_metrics.description: APSR follows COPE guidelines and expects authors to consider reproducibility and reliability prior to submission because published papers may be subject to high-profile scrutiny, replication attempts, and post-publication debate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should consider whether findings are reproducible, how robust they are to different design choices (measurement, sample, specification, estimator), and openly acknowledge weaknesses, assumptions, and limitations. The journal encourages post-publication engagement and corrective measures where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary materials policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary materials (appendices, additional tables/figures, datasets, videos, sound files) that are not essential to the main manuscript may be submitted and will be published online alongside the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplementary materials will be published with the same metadata as the parent article and are a formal part of the academic record: they cannot be retracted or modified except through article correction processes. They will not be typeset or copyedited, so must be supplied exactly as they should appear online. Authors are encouraged to deposit outputs in appropriate repositories and cite them in the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools — authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Generative AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT) do not meet accountability requirements of authorship and must not be listed as authors on submitted content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI tools should never be credited as authors; accountability rests with human authors for all content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of AI tools — declaration requirements (what and when to declare)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must declare and describe use of AI tools when they generate text or images or when used to analyse or extract insights from data or other materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimal, non-generative uses (basic spelling/language checking, single words/brief phrases, minor formatting tasks) do not require declaration. When unsure, contact the editorial office. Accountability for any use of AI rests with the author; check carefully for unintended consequences, especially in references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of AI tools — where to declare
rubrics_metrics.description: Declarations of AI use should appear where other assistance is declared: acknowledgments, a footnote, methods section, or figure captions as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If AI was used to generate text, declare in acknowledgments or footnote. If used to collect/analyze data, describe in methods. If used to generate/modify visual content, declare in figure captions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of AI tools — how to declare (required content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Declarations should include the name and version of the tool, dates used, how the tool can be accessed, a full description of how it was used, and appropriate citations to third-party materials used in the tool's outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additionally include proprietary information, modifications made (e.g., training on own data), and any competing interests or potential biases arising from the tool's use or ownership. Be as specific as reasonably possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility requirements (WCAG 2.1 AA and alt-text)
rubrics_metrics.description: All articles published by Cambridge must meet Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 Level AA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should consider colour use, contrast, text clarity, and provide image descriptions or alt-text for all figures and multimedia. Authors are encouraged to prepare accessibility materials using the Cambridge guide and submission form. If not provided, machine-generated materials will be created but authors are responsible for checking accuracy at proof stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labelling conventions for illustrative material
rubrics_metrics.description: All illustrative materials should be referred to as 'Figures'; tables and figures must be cited in text, numbered consecutively in Arabic numerals, and captions must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diagrams, graphs, maps, boxes, graphical diagrams, and code snippets must also be labelled and numbered. For appendices, letter the items (Table A.1 etc.). See Preparing Accessible Materials guide for detailed instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review transfer policies (transfer out and transfer in)
rubrics_metrics.description: APSR allows transfer of manuscripts and reviews to/from participating journals within specified rules to speed review and reduce reviewer workload.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfer out: After rejection with reviews, authors have 4 weeks to request transfer to participating journal; managing editor initiates transfer and sends anonymized manuscript and reviews. Transfer in: APSR will accept transfers of anonymous manuscripts and identified reviews from other journals that permit transfers; authors should submit a new submission and request the other journal send manuscript and reviews to apsr@apsanet.org within 4 weeks of rejection. Consult recipient journal policies and include a cover letter describing changes. Editors may consult prior reviewers but are not obliged to rely on external reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter (optional uses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover letters are optional and may address issues not handled in the manuscript such as overlap with other work, suggestions for reviewers, or confidentiality concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may use the cover letter to explain special considerations for reviewer selection or to explain why certain information is withheld for confidentiality reasons (where necessary).
